clues.text: Agnes knows Moonmart's old owner and the shop's strange hours.
Pip appears in the shop but not in the window's reflection.
The register holds a receipt for strawberry milk dated 1974.
An old shop photograph shows someone who looks exactly like Pip.
Pip remembers Moonmart as a safe place, though not their own name.
Fern can hear a silence moving through the forest roots.
Lucien carries the same worn detective novel every week.
Wren's map marks a station that vanishes when the ink dries.
The quiet grows strongest at the roots beneath the old grove.
Birdsong has returned to Whisperwood after the grove was tended.
A dedication in Lucien's book is signed simply, 'For Lucien — Ada'.
Lucien has written a letter to Ada that asks only whether she would like to talk.
Wren's sister boarded a late train and never arrived at the station.
A ticket from between places carries Wren's family mark.
A face in the shop photograph is fading, although the frame is untouched.
The letter has a postmark, but no recipient or street address.
The passenger remembers the sea and the smell of bread, but not his name.
The Conductor recalls passengers whose names are missing from Bellwether.
The town archive skips a night in every record from the same year.
Several generations of maps leave a blank where a whole street should be.
Osric's name has been carefully written back into the old town ledger.
The Conductor remembers a promise to keep a place for the lost.
The ticket is stamped for the Midnight Platform, in blue ink that glows faintly.
The platform lies between two stations that are nowhere near each other.
The passenger manifest includes names missing from town records.
Old photographs show Miso keeping watch at Moonmart across many decades.
The Conductor says the guardian's promise never took away Miso's choice.
The light crosses the water toward a place no ordinary chart records.
Elias's log describes a night when the beam guided people from an impossible shore.
The old lens is intact but lacks a small prism to gather its scattered light.
Moonmart was opened so travellers could rest before choosing where to go.
With the lens restored, the beam marks a safe route without pulling anyone along it.
The agreement promises shelter to any traveller who asks for it.
Every traveller is asked whether they want to stay, leave, or keep travelling.
Miso is free to keep the watch or finally curl up and rest.
The boundary can remain open, be shared openly, or close with everyone remembered.
The new covenant records each traveller's right to choose their own way.
A little hidden door has appeared where Miso kept looking.
Under moonlight, Elias's log reveals a second instruction: the lens must be turned toward a willing memory.
A faint note in the ledger says the first keeper never chose which travellers should stay.
The photograph holds a moonlit memory of Miso waiting beside the doorway by choice.
A blue sea-glass bead on the washed shore has a small hole worn smooth by string.
The net-mender recognizes the bead's old sailor's knot: a local wish for every boat to return safely.
A matching blue bead is tied beneath the empty boat's seat beside a tag with no name, only a little drawing of a returning moon.
